item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q020_syntaxin_fragment_reclassification","answer":"In SCOPe 2.08 the early syntaxin entries are not independent complete folds: 1br0 chain A is d1br0a_ and 1ez3 chains A, B, and C are d1ez3a_, d1ez3b_, and d1ez3c_, all classified in class a, All alpha proteins; fold a.47, STAT-like; superfamily a.47.2, t-snare proteins; family a.47.2.1, t-snare proteins; and the rat Syntaxin 1A N-terminal-domain protein node. The important present-day caveat is that each of those 1br0/1ez3 domains is explicitly annotated as a three-helical fragment similar to one spectrin repeat and carries the SCOPe `ms` inconsistency, meaning secondary structures totaling less than one third of the common domain are missing. 1dn1 chain B, d1dn1b_, is also in a.47.2.1, but it sits under SCOPe's automated-match branch as a match to the replacement full-domain syntaxin chain d3c98b_ and has no `ms` fragment warning. Biologically, therefore, the fragment assignments should be interpreted as partial observations of the Syntaxin 1A/t-SNARE family fold, not as full domain definitions and not as permission to transfer complete Syntaxin 1A boundaries, domain count, or exocytotic t-SNARE function from any arbitrary match to the short three-helix core. Same-family placement among d1br0a_, d1ez3a_/b_/c_, d1dn1b_, and d3c98b_ is strong homology evidence inside a.47.2.1, whereas sharing only the broader STAT-like fold a.47 with another protein would be structural evidence at fold strength and would not by itself establish homology or justify using the fragment structures as representatives for whole-domain modeling;
